entities.name: Paulinus of York
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Paulinus of York (d. 644) was a Roman missionary of the Gregorian mission and the first Bishop of York, central to the conversion of King Edwin of Northumbria and the early organisation of the northern English church. Sent from Rome in the second wave of Augustine’s mission, he worked in Kent before accompanying Æthelburh north and baptising Edwin around 627.

His episcopate tied Northumbria to Latin Christendom through stone churches, Roman liturgy, and metropolitan claims for York. After Edwin’s death in 633, political collapse forced Paulinus south again; he ended his career as Bishop of Rochester while the northern mission was rebuilt under Aidan and others.

Paulinus marks the Roman strand of Northumbrian Christianisation later woven together with Irish-influenced Lindisfarne traditions.
